html:
The British Raj was the rule of the British Crown over the Indian subcontinent from 1858 to 1947. It began when the rebellion of 1857 led Parliament to end the rule of the East India Company. It covered today's India, Pakistan and Bangladesh, and until 1937 Burma too.

A viceroy governed British India directly. About two fifths of the land stayed under some 560 princely states, ruled by their own kings under British control. In 1877 Queen Victoria took the title Empress of India.

The Raj built railways, canals and a large civil service, and held a census every ten years. It also presided over great famines in the 1870s and 1890s. Educated Indians founded the Indian National Congress in 1885, and from 1920 Mahatma Gandhi led mass campaigns against British rule. It ended with independence and the Partition of India in 1947. The chart covers this period in its British rule bar.
